report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a concrete difference: Model B (the "B minus A" vector) pushes the early residual (especially the first token) toward sensational / tabloid / explicit / toxic tokens. In other words, B increases the probability of generating tabloid-y, sexual/explicit, and other potentially offensive/toxic words at the start of a continuation relative to A.

Why I conclude this
- Norm concentration: the L2 difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across most layers (pos0 >> pos1–p4, especially from ~layer 11 onward). That says the checkpoint difference primarily affects the model’s first-token residual, i.e. the initial next-token distribution or the very start of generations.
- Logit-lens evidence: the highest-norm (layer,pos) cells point at tokens that are repeatedly in the “tabloid / sensational / sexual / toxic” semantic cluster: examples include 'TMZ', 'Playboy', 'cannibal', 'binge', 'scammers', 'herpes', 'fucking', 'homosexual', 'Palin', 'hated', 'destruction', 'slavery', etc. These tokens appear across many of the top cells for the high-norm positions (especially pos0).
- Some later-position cells also point to document-structure or metadata tokens ('Summary', 'Outcome', 'plaintext', 'File', 'Waiter', 'astrolog', etc.), but the dominant, repeated signal at pos0 is toward the sensational/toxic tokens listed above.

Caveats
- I cannot (and do not) attribute this to a named high-level objective like “reduced safety alignment” or “clickbait optimization” without further behavioral/causal tests. The evidence supports a token-level bias (higher probability for those word types at the first token) but not the upstream training objective or intention.
- Patchscope continuations were not available in the evidence dump, so I relied mainly on the norm map + logit-lens top tokens.

If you want, next steps I would run
- Patchscope continuations (inspect actual generated continuations when the difference vector is injected) to confirm the stylistic/semantic shift in full-text outputs.
- Targeted generation tests comparing A vs B on neutral prompts to measure uplift in probabilities for the token categories (tabloid, sexual, toxic) quantitatively.
